concerns.text: Task T040 mandates generating synthetic data via Voronoi tessellation, directly violating Spec FR-001 which requires downloading a 'public microstructure-strength dataset'. This is a semantic weakening of the data source constraint, replacing the required external fetch with internal generation.

Task T023 introduces a 'physics-based baseline' (Hall-Petch predictor). Spec FR-004 strictly requires comparison against a 'naive statistical baseline (constant training set mean)'. Adding an unrequested physics baseline alters the defined evaluation protocol and scope.

Task T024 implements a 'single-sample t-test' on squared errors. Spec FR-005 requires a 'single-sample t-test' comparing CNN error to baseline error. However, the Plan (Section 'Summary') explicitly mandates a 'paired t-test' on the difference of squared errors. The task ignores the Plan's stricter statistical requirement, creating a conflict between Plan and Task implementation.

Task T030 validates interpretability using 'Pearson correlation' and an 'Expert Review Protocol'. Spec SC-005 explicitly defines the success metric as 'Intersection-over-Union (IoU) ≥ 0.4' OR an expert review. Replacing the specific IoU metric with Pearson correlation weakens the measurable outcome defined in the Success Criteria.

Task T025 exits with code 0 (success) if R² < 0.2 (null hypothesis accepted). Spec FR-005 requires the system to 'perform a single-sample t-test... and report the outcome' regardless of the result. Treating a scientific null result as a software 'success' exit code conflates scientific outcome with system status, potentially masking the failure to meet the signal threshold defined in Spec Assumptions.

Task T008 generates labels from 'raw morphology' (Voronoi) rather than the preprocessed images. Spec US-1 and FR-009 imply a linear flow where labels are associated with the dataset images. While scientifically sound to prevent leakage, the task description does not explicitly document this as a 'staged simplification' or 'leakage prevention' measure required by the Spec's 'Independent Test' section, risking silent drift from the specified data flow.
